facts.text: Boulders on the slope below the summit shift underfoot, and very loose rock sits just under the top.
Mapped summit marks are misplaced; the true top lies northeast of them, so aim past the mapped point.
In late August a traverse from the last long switchback below the Doelle pass was less sustained than the boulder field direct from the upper lake.
The easiest top-out is a counter-clockwise corkscrew starting from the north-northwest ridge; only the final 200 ft is semi-exposed class 3.
At the end of June snow still lies on the upper slopes, so expect to kick steps.
By the end of September fresh snow can coat the slopes above about 6,400 ft.
Mill Creek Road 6960 is rough and steep; in a high-clearance rig a party parked near 3,900 ft, about 1.25 miles from the PCT, and a sedan will struggle.
In the dark at the end of September the PCT crossing is easy to walk over without noticing; check the map before leaving the road.

notes: The South Ridge row has no trailhead or summit pin and no qualifying track. Standard-route pins agree with Peakbagger (summit 13 m).
